---
title: "SAWA: an open real-time antiretroviral-resistance surveillance platform for sub-Saharan Africa"
author:
  - name: Kelyn Njeri
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000  # replace when issued
    email: kelyn@neoforge.io
    affiliations:
      - name: NeoForge Labs, Nairobi, Kenya
abstract: |
  We present SAWA (Sub-Saharan Africa Watch for Antiretroviral
  resistance), an open, reproducible pipeline for continuous HIV-1
  drug-resistance surveillance from public sequence data (LANL,
  GenBank), designed for the subtypes (A1, C, D) that dominate East
  African epidemics. The pipeline calls resistance against Stanford
  HIVdb, builds subtype-stratified phylogenies, detects transmission
  clusters using the CDC HIV-TRACE convention, and exposes results
  through a public dashboard. On a laptop, the full East African cohort
  (~25 000 sequences, six countries, three decades) processes in under
  90 minutes end-to-end. Every figure in this paper regenerates from raw
  data via `make paper1`; every headline claim maps to a benchmark
  script under `benchmarks/`. We demonstrate the platform's utility on
  three case studies: (i) the pan-East-African resistance landscape
  2005–2023, (ii) parity of our custom distance clusterer with
  HIV-TRACE against simulated ground truth, and (iii) first detection
  of emerging INSTI resistance in A1/D following the 2019 WHO
  dolutegravir rollout.
keywords:

# Results

## Pan-East-African resistance landscape

![Resistance landscape across country × year × drug class, stratified
by subtype. Cells with N < 5 are shown grey.](figures/fig02_resistance_landscape.pdf){#fig-landscape}

@fig-landscape shows resistance prevalence across `${N_COUNTRIES}`
countries and `${N_YEARS}` years.

## Cluster parity with HIV-TRACE

![Cluster detection precision/recall/F1 against simulated ground truth,
our distance clusterer vs HIV-TRACE.](figures/fig03_cluster_validation.pdf){#fig-cluster}

@fig-cluster demonstrates cluster-detection parity against the CDC
HIV-TRACE reference tool on synthetic transmission networks with known
membership.

## DTG-era INSTI resistance in East Africa

![INSTI major-mutation prevalence pre- vs post-2019 dolutegravir
rollout, stratified by subtype.](figures/fig04_dtg_case_study.pdf){#fig-dtg}

@fig-dtg presents the biological headline of this paper: emerging INSTI
resistance in East African A1/D subtypes following the 2019 WHO
first-line switch to dolutegravir.

## Scalability

![Pipeline wall time vs input sequence count, log-log. Power-law
exponents annotated per stage.](figures/fig05_scalability.pdf){#fig-scale}

@fig-scale reports scaling of each pipeline stage. On the reference
hardware (${HOST_PLATFORM}, ${CPU_COUNT} cores), fitted exponents are
close to 1.0 for ingestion and alignment, and approach 2.0 for
clustering as expected from tn93's pairwise-distance complexity.
